event: Nala sleeps in the back room with the rain on the roof.
She wakes to grey light and rain, puts the kettle on and goes back to the table.
She trues every seam line of the paper pattern against the figures in her book.
She lets the toile out at the hip by a hair, where it would pull.
She presses the silk, and it lies flat on the cutting table, ready for the shears.

memory.fact: The silk takes an iron's heat without a mark.

event: By noon she has her finest needles and a silk thread matched to the grey-green.
The rain keeps on; when it grows too dark to sew by, Nala lights the lamps.
The bell rings; Shaestrel comes in through the bolted door again.

memory.fact: She will return on April 29 when the lamps are lit, for the gown's first fitting.

event: She looks at the calico toile and says it's the colour of porridge.
She unpins her cloak.
Nala tells her porridge is great and she means to make her look delicious, and winks.
Shaestrel laughs, and says 'delicious' back slowly, as if tasting it.
She hooks a finger in Nala's apron string and draws her a step closer.
She tugs her shoulder cords, and her dress falls about her feet as birch leaves.

memory.fact: Her pale green dress was glamour, and fell from her as fresh birch leaves.

event: She lifts the calico toile off its hook herself.
She holds it out to Nala and tells her to dress her, then.
Nala eases the calico toile over Shaestrel's head; she wrinkles her nose and holds still.
Nala pins the forward shoulder seam back, fingers trailing to her collarbone after.
She takes the sides in under the arm and smooths the calico over her ribs, slowly.
Shaestrel lets her; Nala's hands stay at her waist a breath after the last pin.
Nala kneels to pin the hem and runs a palm down the back of her calf.

memory.fact: Nala pinned the calico toile on Shaestrel at the gown's first fitting, on the evening of April 29.

event: Shaestrel hums her low quick tune, and it catches when Nala's hand reaches her ankle.
When Nala rises to check the waist, Shaestrel lays a hand over hers.
She says Nala has pinned this waist twice, and keeps Nala's hand where it is.
Nala says she can't be sure it fits, and could check it all again more thoroughly.
Shaestrel repeats 'more thoroughly' and calls it a fine word.
She lets go of Nala's hand, takes the tape from her neck and loops it round her waist.
Her knuckles rest on Nala's ribs as she reads the figure, head tipped.
She says she has Nala's measure now as well.

memory.fact: She took Nala's waist measure with Nala's own tape on April 29, and said she has her measure now.
She took Nala's waist measure with Nala's own tape on April 29, and said she has her measure now.

event: She says thoroughly can wait for the silk, and tucks the tape back round Nala's neck.
Nala says it's time she started on the silk.
Nala lifts the pinned calico off Shaestrel, who wraps herself in her grey cloak.
Shaestrel sits on the edge of the cutting table and says she'd like to see the first cut.
Nala unpicks the toile and carries each pinned change onto the paper pattern.
She lays the silk out, pins the paper to it and cuts the gown's pieces with her shears.

memory.fact: Nala cut the gown's pieces from the silk on the night of April 29, with Shaestrel watching.

event: Shaestrel watches the whole while, chin on her knees, her eyes on the shears.
When the last piece comes free, an arm's length of silk is left on the table.

changes.note: Silk cut into the gown's pieces; an arm's length spare
changes.to: Grey-green silk cut into the pieces of the gown, with an arm's length left over.

memory.fact: The bolt holds enough silk for one gown, with about an arm's length to spare.

event: Shaestrel drapes the spare length over Nala's shoulders and says it suits her hair.
Nala thanks her; if she wants the hair as an accessory, she'll have to bring Nala to the ball.
Shaestrel laughs and winds a lock of Nala's hair round one finger.
She says she'll bring Nala across the ford to the dance on Beltane night.

event: She lets the lock go, takes Nala's hand and kisses her knuckles.
